DACI Memory

Dementia Education, De-Escalation & Crisis Intervention

Understand the person behind distress and adapt support to their remaining abilities. Explore person-centered communication, daily care, and non-physical approaches to preventing and de-escalating dementia-related distress.

← All DACI programs
Dementia & Cognitive Support • Hands-Off

Who this program is for

Memory care, assisted living, skilled nursing, home care, hospice, adult day services, and healthcare teams supporting people living with dementia.

Person-centered, non-physical support for individuals living with dementia and cognitive impairment.

Learning outcomes

  • Recognize how cognitive changes affect daily life.
  • Consider personal history and remaining abilities when planning support.
  • Interpret distress as possible communication of an unmet need.
  • Adapt communication and care to the individual.
  • Use non-physical strategies to reduce distress.
  • Contribute to a consistent person-centered care plan.

Inside the program

Curriculum & Learning Modules

A practical overview of the topics covered in this DACI program.

MODULE 01

Dementia & changing abilities

Connect cognitive changes with practical support needs.

MODULE 02

Knowing the person

Consider preferences, history, strengths, and personhood.

MODULE 03

Behavior as communication

Look for unmet needs and distress triggers.

MODULE 04

Communication that fits

Adapt language and approach as communication abilities change.

MODULE 05

Support during daily care

Match assistance and activities to remaining abilities.

MODULE 06

Preventing & de-escalating distress

Practice person-centered, non-physical responses.

MODULE 07

Supportive environments & relationships

Consider environmental changes and family support.

MODULE 08

Care planning & team follow-through

Translate observations into consistent support approaches.
